look_here_first: Start low on the plant. Gray goldenrod is comparatively short and gray-hairy, with a densely pubescent stem and narrow spatulate-to-oblanceolate lower leaves that become smaller and narrower upward. Then check the usually one-sided, wandlike/recurving flowering branches.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: usually shorter and less colony-forming than tall goldenrods; stem densely short-hairy to gray-pubescent; lower leaves oblanceolate to spatulate and narrowed into a winged petiole; upper leaves progressively smaller and narrower; flowering array often one-sided and wandlike or recurving; common in dry open prairie, caliche, glade, old-field, and roadside settings

key_traits.label: Comparison training
key_traits.text: Compared with Solidago radula, S. nemoralis is more gray/strigose overall and usually has a more wandlike one-sided inflorescence; S. radula is conspicuously scabrous with broader lower leaves and a more compact terminal panicle.

lookalikes.differences: Gray goldenrod combines persistent gray pubescence, narrower lower foliage, and a one-sided wandlike flowering array. Rough goldenrod is more stiffly scabrous and has a more compact terminal panicle.
